title: In-Person Appointments Held by One Patient Over Time
content:
A patient may hold any number of In-Person Appointments over time and across visit types; there is no lifetime cap on appointments.

What is capped is narrower: the number of appointments of one visit type that the patient holds open at the same time. That cap is governed by the open-appointment rule for the visit type, not by any overall count.

Appointments made for family members are separate holdings, each under that family member's own patient profile. They never count toward one another's caps: a parent's open appointments and a child's open appointments are counted separately, each against its own profile.

| Question | Answer under this principle |
|---|---|
| Is there a limit on how many appointments a patient may have over a lifetime? | No. |
| Is there a limit on appointments held open at once? | Yes, per visit type, under the open-appointment rule. |
| Do a family member's appointments count toward the caller's own cap? | No; each patient's appointments sit under that patient's own profile. |

*Hypothetical illustration:* a parent books an Established Patient Office Visit for herself and another for her son. Each booking is counted only under the profile of the patient it is for.
